column1: # Where a subspecies or variety can occur, by island.
# NZTCS assesses many subspecies and varieties separately but carries no
# distribution field. A record identified only to species could then be any of
# them, and the choice can change its threat status. Where the taxa are
# separated by island, the record's own coordinates settle it.
# taxon      the NZTCS name, exactly as NZTCS writes it
# allow      where it occurs, comma-separated. Occurd derives these zones from a
#              Codfish               nearshore islands; a record there is also NI
#              Kermadec, ThreeKings, Chatham, Snares, AucklandIslands, Campbell,
#              Antipodes, Bounty     outlying islands; a record there is in that
#            Finer mainland zones (Northland, SIWest, SIEast, Foveaux ...) are
#            kept on some rows for reference. Occurd does not derive them yet,
#            so those taxa are never picked automatically and the question is
#              none  not expected as a wild record anywhere in New Zealand
# certainty  certain -> out of range rules the taxon out
#            check   -> out of range makes it the last choice, not an impossible one
# instead    optional; not used by Occurd
# A taxon with no row is treated as possible everywhere.
# --- birds: subspecies that a bare binomial has to choose between ---

Tainui. Naturally from scattered sites on the western North Island coast between Kawhia Harbour and Mohakatino; now only Mokau and the Mohakatino River mouth. It has naturalised well in the drier eastern South Island, on Stewart Island and around Wellington, Napier, Hamilton and Cambridge, but NZTCS assesses the wild population, so a naturalised plant is not the Nationally Critical taxon
